problems.title: Intersect a parabola and a line
problems.question: Solve x²=18−3x graphically.
problems.idea: The solutions are the intersection abscissas of y=x² and y=18−3x.
steps: The graphs meet at (−6,36) and (3,9), as substitution confirms.
Their x-coordinates solve the equation.

problems.title: The greatest altitude
problems.question: A triangle has sides 3,6,8. Find its greatest altitude.
problems.idea: The greatest altitude belongs to the shortest side.
steps: All altitudes have the same numerator 2Δ, so use base 3.
The greatest altitude is (√935/2)/3.

problems.title: A quadratic with radical coefficients
problems.question: Solve x²+(5√3−3)x+20−7√3=0.
problems.idea: Look for factors whose roots have the required sum and product.
steps: Compute the discriminant: D=(5√3−3)²−4(20−7√3)=4−2√3=(√3−1)².
The two values simplify to 1−2√3 and 2−3√3.

problems.title: A rectangle under a parabola
problems.question: A rectangle has two vertices on y=x² and two on the x-axis. Its perimeter is 30 cm. Find its sides.
problems.idea: The upper vertices have equal height, hence opposite x-coordinates.
formulas: Let upper vertices be (−t,t²),(t,t²), t>0. Sides are 2t and t².
steps: Choose t=3.

problems.title: Construct a triangle from two angles and perimeter
problems.question: Construct a triangle given two angles and its perimeter p.
problems.idea: Build any triangle with those angles, then scale it.
formulas: Similar triangles have equal angles and proportional corresponding lengths and perimeters.
steps: Construct a temporary triangle A₀B₀C₀ using the two prescribed angles; their sum must be less than 180°.
Construct a segment equal to its perimeter p₀ by laying its three sides end to end.
By a parallel-line proportional construction, scale side A₀B₀ by p/p₀ to obtain AB.
At A and B copy the prescribed angles; their rays meet at C. Its perimeter is (p/p₀)p₀=p.
problems.answer: The resulting triangle has the required angles and perimeter; it is unique up to congruence for positive p and valid angles.

problems.title: A section through intersecting diagonals
problems.question: A right trapezoid has shorter leg √7 and diagonals 4,√43. Find the segment parallel to its bases through the diagonal intersection.
problems.idea: Recover both bases using right triangles, then use the harmonic-mean section.
steps: The shorter leg is its height. The diagonal equations therefore give bases 3 and 6.
The diagonal intersection divides the height in ratio 3:6. The parallel section length is 2·3·6/(3+6).

problems.title: Simplify a radical fraction with its domain
problems.question: Simplify $\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{2-a}}{2-a+\sqrt{2-a}}-\frac{1-\sqrt{2-a}}{2-a-\sqrt{2-a}}\right)\sqrt{2/a-1}$ for $0<a<2$.
problems.idea: Put t=√(2−a) and cancel factors carefully.
steps: The two fractions reduce to 1/t and −1/t respectively, provided t≠1.
Their difference is 2/t, and multiplication by t/√a gives 2/√a.
The original denominator vanishes at t=1, or a=1, which must remain excluded.
problems.note: The stated interval alone overlooks the undefined point a=1.

problems.title: Prove a strict rational inequality
problems.question: Prove a/b²+b/a²>1/a+1/b if a+b>0, a≠b, ab>0.
problems.idea: Subtract the right side and factor.
steps: The denominator is positive because ab≠0.
The numerator is positive because a+b>0 and a≠b.
Therefore the difference is strictly positive.

problems.title: A chord of contact for two internal tangents
problems.question: Two circles have centers 15 cm apart. Their common internal tangents meet at K; KA=3 cm and KD=2 cm. Find the contact chord AC on the first circle.
problems.idea: The tangent right triangles at K are similar.
formulas: Let KO₁=u, KO₂=v. Then u/v=3/2 and u+v=15.
steps: Thus u=9,v=6. The first radius r=√(9²−3²)=6√2.
In right triangle KO₁A, the distance from A to O₁K is KA·r/KO₁=3·6√2/9=2√2.
The contact chord AC is perpendicular to O₁K and bisected by it, so AC=2·2√2.

problems.title: Exactly one root including degenerate cases
problems.question: Find every a for which a(2a+4)x²−(a+2)x−5a−10=0 has exactly one real solution.
problems.idea: Factor the parameter, then distinguish a quadratic from a linear equation.
steps: At a=−2 every x works, so exclude it. At a=0 the equation is linear and gives x=−5.
For a≠0,−2 the discriminant is 1+40a. Exactly one real root requires a=−1/40.
At that value the double root is x=1/(4a)=−10.
